question: Should ClawHub adopt an advisory-first, trust-boundary capability manifest for skills, and which authority and legacy-compatibility model should govern it?
rationale: The proposal adds a public security contract rather than repairing an established broken behavior; maintainers must choose the permanent schema boundary, whether declarations are self-attested or verified, and the adoption path before implementation can be safely scoped.

options.title: Adopt an advisory-first contract
options.body: Specify a narrow capability schema, retain legacy skills without a declaration, and use discrepancies only to inform review until accuracy and policy are proven.

options.title: Defer to existing metadata
options.body: Keep environment-variable and dependency declarations as the current visibility mechanism and decline a broader capability contract for now.

options.title: Design alongside review policy
options.body: First align this RFC with the separate cross-asset and agent-directed-instruction policy proposals, then adopt one coordinated trust model.

recommendation.title: Adopt an advisory-first contract
recommendation.body: Specify a narrow capability schema, retain legacy skills without a declaration, and use discrepancies only to inform review until accuracy and policy are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the closest merged manifest surface and are the strongest history-based routing candidate for the compatibility implications.
